m.chalisa.do1: Victory, victory to Mother Śītalā. Whoever meditates on you, his heart becomes pure and cool, and his intellect, strength and knowledge blossom.
m.chalisa.do2: Śītalā, dweller in every heart, your radiance is cool. In the cool shade the Mother hangs a cradle and rocks it.
m.chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory, victory to Śītalā Bhavānī. Victory to the mother of the world, a mine of every virtue.
m.chalisa.cau2: Your power shines in every home, adorned like the full autumn moon.
m.chalisa.cau3: The body burning with smallpox you make cool, and you take away all its pain.
m.chalisa.cau4: Mother Śītalā, your auspicious name comes to the help of all in hard times.
m.chalisa.cau5: You are the remover of grief, Śaṅkarī, Bhavānī, protector of children's lives and giver of happiness.
m.chalisa.cau6: A pure broom and a water-pot grace your hands; on your forehead a splendour shines like the sun.
m.chalisa.cau7: The sixty-four yoginīs sing with you and play the vīṇā, cymbals and mṛdaṅga.
m.chalisa.cau8: Lord Bhairava displays his dance; not even Śeṣa and Śiva easily find your end.
m.chalisa.cau9: Blessed, blessed are you, the nurturing mother, the great queen; gods, men and sages proclaim your fair fame.
m.chalisa.cau10: There was a huge demon, Visphoṭaka, in the form of flame and mighty in strength.
m.chalisa.cau11: He entered house after house and no one could protect them; taking the form of disease, he devoured children.
m.chalisa.cau12: A great outcry arose throughout the world, when no one could avert the calamity.
m.chalisa.cau13: Then the Mother took on a wondrous form, holding a broom and a winnowing basket in her hands.
m.chalisa.cau14: She seized Visphoṭaka with her hand and struck him with a pestle in many ways.
m.chalisa.cau15: He pleaded in many ways: Mother, I did not rightly know you at all.
m.chalisa.cau16: Mother, I shall not now go into anyone's house; where there is impurity, all its sorrow will be taken away.
m.chalisa.cau17: Burning bodies will become cool, and the dread terror of smallpox will perish.
m.chalisa.cau18: Worship of Śrī Śītalā brings welfare: the Lord has spoken this true word.
m.chalisa.cau19: Brother, the house where there is fear of smallpox should worship the Goddess; this is the remedy.
m.chalisa.cau20: Let it have a kalaśa of Śītalā adorned, and have a Brahmin recite the text according to the rite.
m.chalisa.cau21: Śītalā, you alone are the mother of the world, you alone the father, the giver of joy to the world.
m.chalisa.cau22: You alone are the sustainer of the world, giver of joy to those who serve you. Salutations, I bow to you, Goddess Śītalā.
m.chalisa.cau23: Salutations to you who give happiness and take away sorrow; salutations, salutations to you, the boat that carries the world across.
m.chalisa.cau24: Salutations, salutations to you, revered by the three worlds, uprooter of sorrow, poverty and the rest.
m.chalisa.cau25: You are Śrī Śītalā, Śeṛhalā, Mahalā, Ruṇalīhyuṇanī and Mother Mandalā.
m.chalisa.cau26: You bear a sky-clad body; your mount of five names looks splendid.
m.chalisa.cau27: It is the donkey: rāsabha, khara, vaiśākha-sunandana, gardabha, the uprooter of dūrvā roots.
m.chalisa.cau28: Whoever remembers Mother Śītalā, at that very remembrance all his sorrows flee far away.
m.chalisa.cau29: Whatever swelling of the throat, goitre or the like there may be, for it there is no mantra and no medicine.
m.chalisa.cau30: There is only the worship of the Mother; there is no other means.
m.chalisa.cau31: Whoever comes to the Mother's refuge with firm faith becomes fearless and gains the fruit his heart desires.
m.chalisa.cau32: The leper gains a spotless body, and the blind man sees with his own eyes.
m.chalisa.cau33: The childless woman gains a son, and one poor from birth becomes rich.
m.chalisa.cau34: Singing the virtues of Mother Śītalā, even the mute has been seen composing verse.
m.chalisa.cau35: Let no one have any doubt in this: throughout the world it is the Mother's drum alone that sounds.
m.chalisa.cau36: Says Rāmasundara Prabhudāsa: on the bank, to the east of Prayāga, close by,
m.chalisa.cau37: Purī Tivārī is my home, at Kakarā on the bank of the Gaṅgā, by Durvāsā's hermitage.
m.chalisa.cau38: Now it grows late; I call to you, Mother, watching the road for your grace.
m.chalisa.cau39: This perishable one lies here with his hope set on you; protect me, Mother Śītalā.
